    gh add repo reponame    //git@github.com:<user>/newrepo --public
    git remote  origin set ...  //url
    git push origin -u main

Below is a ready‑to‑copy **`.gitignore`** for a Go project that uses **Fyne** (the Go GUI toolkit).  
It also explicitly ignores the `history.json` file you mentioned.

```gitignore
# ---------- Go ----------
# Binaries for programs and libraries
*.exe
*.exe~
*.dll
*.so
*.dylib

# Test binary, built with `go test -c`
*.test

# Output of the go coverage tool, when used with `go test -coverprofile`
*.out

# Build artefacts
/build
/bin
/obj
/dist

# Go workspace file
go.work
go.work.sum

# Dependency directories (if vendoring)
vendor/

# ---------- Fyne ----------
# Fyne caches the compiled UI assets in a hidden folder
.fyne-cache/
.fyne-state/

# Fyne generated assets (e.g. when using `fyne bundle`)
*.fynebundle
*.fynebundle.go

# Fyne generated icons / resources (if you keep them in the repo)
# (Uncomment if you generate temporary icons)
# /icons/

# ---------- IDE / Editor ----------
# VS Code
.vscode/
*.code-workspace

# GoLand / IntelliJ
.idea/
*.iml

# Sublime Text
*.sublime-project
*.sublime-workspace

# Vim
*.swp
*.swo
*~

# Emacs
*~
\#*\#
.#*

# ---------- OS ----------
# macOS
.DS_Store
.AppleDouble
.LSOverride

# Linux
*~

# Windows
Thumbs.db
ehthumbs.db
Desktop.ini
$RECYCLE.BIN/

# ---------- Misc ----------
# Logs
*.log

# Local configuration files
.env
.env.*

# History file you asked for
history.json
```

## CLI workflow – from an empty folder to a pushed GitHub repo

> **Assumptions**  
> * You have **Git** installed and configured (`git config --global user.name …` etc.).  
> * You have the **GitHub CLI** (`gh`) installed and authenticated (`gh auth login`).  
> * Replace `<USER>` and `<REPO>` with your GitHub username/organization and the desired repository name.

```bash
# 1️⃣ Initialise a new git repository
git init

# 2️⃣ (Optional) Create the main branch name you want (Git 2.28+ defaults to 'main')
git branch -M main

# 3️⃣ Add everything (including the .gitignore you just created)
git add .

# 4️⃣ First commit
git commit -m "msg : initial init"

# 5️⃣ Create the GitHub repository via the GitHub CLI
#    - `--public` makes it public; drop for a private repo.
#    - `--source=.` tells gh the current folder is the repo source.
#    - `--remote=origin` creates the remote named "origin".
gh repo create <REPO> --public --source=. --remote=origin

#   (If you prefer to create the repo on the GitHub website first,
#    you can skip the `gh repo create` step and set the remote manually,
#    see step 6.)

# 6️⃣ (If you created the repo elsewhere) Point the local repo to the remote URL
#    Use SSH (as in your example) – replace <USER> with your GitHub login.
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:<USER>/<REPO>.git

# 7️⃣ Push the initial commit to GitHub, establishing the upstream tracking branch
git push -u origin main
```

### What each command does

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `git init` | Starts a new empty Git repository in the current directory. |
| `git branch -M main` | Renames the default branch to `main` (if it isn’t already). |
| `git add .` | Stages **all** files (including the `.gitignore`). |
| `git commit -m "msg : initial init"` | Records the first snapshot with your message. |
| `gh repo create …` | Calls the GitHub API to create a new remote repository and automatically adds it as `origin`. |
| `git remote set-url origin …` | (If you didn’t use `gh repo create`) Manually points `origin` at the SSH URL of the newly‑created repo. |
| `git push -u origin main` | Sends the local `main` branch to GitHub and sets the upstream so future `git push`/`git pull` work without extra arguments. |

---

### Quick one‑liner (if you *already* have the GitHub repo created)

```bash
git init && git branch -M main && git add . && git commit -m "msg : initial init" && \
git remote add origin git@github.com:<USER>/<REPO>.git && git push -u origin main
```

That’s it—your Go + Fyne workspace is now version‑controlled and hosted on GitHub! 🎉
